To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the magnocellular (MC) pathway is a high-speed channel for the detection of visual motion, that it is a parallel channel to the parvocellular (PC) pathway for the detection of fine detail, and that it is the only pathway for detecting the direction of motion.

(1) the primate visual pathway contains a parallel processing hierarchy of multiple channels and (2) that the primate visual cortex has an anatomical and functional organization based on the segregation of these channels.
(1) the magnocellular pathway is more important than the parvocellular pathway for visual attention, and (2) the magnocelluar and parvocellular pathways have different roles in visual perception.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the brain processes visual information, and the role of the thalamus in this.
the neural basis of vision, and the way in which we use visual information to guide our behaviour.
how the primate brain processes the visual world, and how this processing might be disrupted by brain injury.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the visual system is organized to signal two fundamental features of visual information, colour and fine detail, and movement and visual distance, respectively, and that this organization is achieved by a dorsal–ventral segregation in the visual pathway.
the parvocellular pathway is the main route for colour processing, whereas the magnocellular pathway is mainly involved in movement detection and depth perception.
the parvocellular pathway is responsible for colour vision and the magnocellular pathway for motion perception.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dorsal stream of visual information, the pathway that leads to the parietal cortex, has a major role in visual perception.
we have found a new mechanism for the visual cortex to process information.
the dorsal stream of the visual system (V1–MT) is a motion-processing pathway, whereas the ventral stream (V1–IT) is a form-processing pathway.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the primate visual brain has a rich repertoire of mechanisms for extracting and processing the visual world.
the visual system is not a passive transducer but an active information processing system.
there are two distinct types of visual information, which we call “what” and “where” information.
